draft.title: Sexual and asexual reproduction
card: One parent makes offspring. There is no fusion of gametes (sex cells), so the offspring are genetically identical to the parent, apart from rare mutations.
Two parents each make gametes, and these fuse. The offspring get a mix of genes from both parents, so they differ from each parent and from each other.
Asexual reproduction is usually fast and needs no mate. It can fill a stable habitat quickly, but a single disease or change in conditions may harm every identical individual.
Sexual reproduction is slower and needs a mate. The variation it gives means some offspring may survive when conditions change.
draft.remember: Asexual: one parent, identical offspring, fast. Sexual: two parents, variation.

a.q: Which feature of sexual reproduction gives variation in offspring?
opts: Genes from two parents are combined
Offspring are made by one parent alone
Offspring are made without gametes
Offspring copy the genes of the parent
a.why: Gametes from two parents fuse, so the offspring get a new mix of genes. In asexual reproduction one parent passes on its genes unchanged, so the offspring are identical.
a.clue: Think about how many parents give genes.

b.q: A disease strikes a farm of potato plants grown from pieces of one parent plant. Every plant dies. Which reason best explains this?
opts: The plants were identical, so all were equally at risk
The plants had mixed genes, so all were equally at risk
The plants were made sexually, so they had no variation
The plants were slow to reproduce, so they were weak
b.why: Plants grown from pieces of one parent are made asexually and are genetically identical. If one is open to the disease, all are. The second option is wrong because mixed genes come from sexual reproduction and give variation.
b.clue: Ask how the plants were made and how alike they are.

a.best: Genes from two parents are combined

b.best: The plants were identical, so all were equally at risk

problems.detail: The why refers to 'the second option' (mixed genes), but the options are shuffled and that option appears third here. Students could be pointed to the wrong option. Name the option by its content, not its position.
